newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 5.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- South Korea considers easing requirements needed for China-Based ethnic Koreans to visit Korea as part of measures to help eliminate increasing number of swindling cases perpetrated by some ethnic Koreans seeking job opportunies in South Korea.
- National Assembly expected to delay action on government-initiated labour law revision bill that touched off conflicting reactions from both employers organisations and trade unions.
- Top leader of Federation of Korean Industries recently forwarded a recommendation to President Kim calling for an emergency decree to effectuate a five-year wage freeze.
- Labour law revision bill triggers labor-management tension: labour union vow to stage strikes, but employer organizations expected to join forces to counter labour offensives.
- Defense ministry decides to recollect cash credit cards and pagers from enlisted men to forestall relaxation of military disciplines and leak of military secrets.

- Constitutional amendment designed for altering the form of government in favour of cabinet responsibility would be up for political negotiation next year: opposition leader Kim Dae-jung says in an year-end interview with Chosun Ilbo.
- U.S. negative on Seoul's bid for longer range missiles
- Economic groups call on government to delay multiple union system, and are poised to cope with unions' threats of strike.
- Seoul seeks to buy air-to-ground missiles to enhance aircraft attack capability.
